title: Logical relationships in data structures
summary: Compare four kinds of logical relationships: sequential order, parent-child hierarchy, network connections, and key-value mapping.
description: The left column of the figure groups linear data structures, and the right column groups nonlinear data structures; the hash table spans across the bottom beneath both columns to illustrate key-value mapping separately.

frames.title: Logical relationships in data structures
frames.explanation: Linear structures maintain a sequential order while differing in where operations are permitted; trees and heaps organize parent-child hierarchies, and graphs allow a vertex to connect to multiple neighbors. What is compared here is logical structure rather than underlying physical storage: the same logical relationship can be implemented in different ways, and a hash table can combine arrays, linked lists, or trees.
